cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the overseas job or opening this shop with me. You said we'd build something together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before I got the offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide what together means now. I'll run the counter if you'll still do the accounts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making a job abroad sound like leaving you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your share and do the accounts from there. Or let me buy you out, and I'll stop calling that promise a business plan.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs a binary career choice tied to the old promise, while A3 and A5 offer altered work arrangements to keep B in the project.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 new offer changes A3 roles; B4 leaving objection produces A5 remote accounts and buyout options.

relationship.evidence: B2 legitimately treats a new opportunity as relevant and B4 resists equating career with personal departure.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes the initial physical-presence binary to financial partnership or separation following B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 unopened shop and A5 shares are intelligible, though the final business-plan metaphor makes the demanded choice less immediate.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 stop-calling-promise-business-plan is a reviewer-facing interpretation after two practical requests.
